behavior: When `KeepAlive` deactivates a popup, the popup keeps its open state. It releases the scroll lock, the modal marks, the document listeners and the timers. The portal element of the popup leaves the document. When `KeepAlive` activates the popup again, the popup takes them back, and the same portal element returns. A popup that mounts while `KeepAlive` holds its branch stays out of the document until the activation. Until then it takes no scroll lock, no modal marks and no focus, and it does not close on a press outside it. It reports no open state to a dialog or a drawer above it, or to `Drawer.Provider`. A part below its root can call the handle in `onMounted`, as in a shown branch. The root then detaches from its handle before a detached trigger can follow the handle, and it attaches again at the activation. Its node in the popup tree counts as open only from the activation. At the activation, it takes the place that a popup that mounts in a shown branch has. A part that mounts below the root later, while `KeepAlive` holds the root or after `KeepAlive` deactivated it, can also call the handle in `onMounted`. The root runs that call after its activation, as `Activity` runs the effects of a part at the reveal. A positioner that mounts while `KeepAlive` holds its branch starts its anchor updates at the activation.
